answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying voting weight to one continuous, non-transferable thread of peer-countersigned work. Like copper wire, that thread conducts trust only while it stays unbroken: each completed job extends it, and a failed audit cuts it back to zero. A sparrow of an identity, newly hatched, weighs almost nothing; real influence takes months of graded work. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones must fund and patiently work a thousand separate threads, paying full time and effort per clone - the swarm costs more than the honest path it tries to outvote.
